title: Responsive Images & Media 🖼️

slides.title: Why Responsive Images? 🖥️📱
slides.content:
# One Size Doesn't Fit All

Serving a 2000px‑wide hero image to a 375px phone wastes bandwidth and slows loading. Responsive images allow the browser to download the most appropriate version based on screen size, resolution, or format support.

Two main techniques:
- **Resolution switching** (same image, different sizes) – using `srcset` + `sizes`.
- **Art direction** (different crop/composition) – using `<picture>` and `<source>`.

slides.title: How `srcset` and `sizes` Work 🧠
slides.content:
# Let the Browser Choose

- `srcset` lists image URLs with a **width descriptor** (`480w`).
- `sizes` tells the browser how wide the image slot will be at different viewport conditions (e.g., on small screens the image is 480px wide, otherwise 800px).
- The browser then picks the best fit, also factoring in device pixel ratio (2x, 3x).

This ensures retina screens get high‑res images and low‑res screens get smaller files.

quizData.question: In `srcset`, the notation `800w` means the image is ______ pixels wide.
quizData.explanation: The `w` descriptor tells the browser the image's intrinsic width in CSS pixels, not the viewport width.
